definition.name: Tn5-mediated DNA fragmentation and adapter tagging
definition.substrate: DNA-containing material accessible to adapter-loaded Tn5, including DNA in chromatin; material state and prior enrichment are retained on each use.
definition.operation: Couple DNA fragmentation with introduction of sequencing-adapter tags in a Tn5 transposition reaction.
definition.physical_mechanism: Adapter-loaded hyperactive Tn5 transposase fragments substrate DNA and integrates its adapter payload at insertion sites.
definition.output: Tagmented DNA-containing material carrying sequencing-adapter tags, at the reaction-product stage before separately required purification, end completion or PCR; support and protein association are retained as per-use properties.
definition.information_effect: Adds sequencing-adapter sequence at fragmentation/insertion sites while retaining substrate-derived DNA sequence and fragment information for downstream readout. Which genomic regions are represented and what their representation means depend on upstream selection and substrate accessibility, recorded on each use.
definition.purpose: Generate adapter-tagged DNA fragments for subsequent sequencing-library preparation.
definition.context_requirements: Requires DNA, an adapter-loaded Tn5 preparation and conditions permitting the coupled transposition/tagging reaction. Native versus fixed chromatin, prior antibody enrichment, bead attachment, enzyme product, buffer, dose, duration and downstream readout are contextual properties rather than universal membership conditions.

tn5_dna_fragmentation_adapter_tagging.scope_note: A shared-mechanism concept requiring both DNA fragmentation and sequencing-adapter introduction by Tn5. It spans the supplied native-nuclear and immunoprecipitated bead-chromatin implementations without making either the defining substrate. The assigned transformation ends at tagmented material; later washes, crosslink reversal, DNA purification, end completion and amplification remain separate interfaces. RNA reverse transcription with template-switch handle introduction does not meet this mechanism. Membership establishes neither experimental substitution, shared ancestry, literature novelty nor a complete reaction recipe.
